item.title: The invisible war: Iran's evolving cyberattacks bring battlefront to small-town America
item.description: The escalation of Iran's cyber capabilities in its ongoing tensions with the US and Israel is becoming increasingly pronounced. Recent intrusions into US water facilities mark a transition into a new blend of warfare. These digital strikes bolster military initiatives while attempting to sway international public opinion. Additionally, the infusion of artificial intelligence into these operations allows for unprecedented efficiency and breadth, reinforcing Iran's asymmetric strategies within its military doctrine.

item.title: Govt orders Google to shut down hundreds of Firebase accounts over scam misuse
item.description: Indian authorities ordered Google to close hundreds of Firebase accounts. These accounts were exploited by criminals for banking scams and malware. Officials found a pattern of impersonating major banks to defraud users. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre issued multiple notices for account removals. This action is part of India's increased efforts against online financial fraud.

item.title: Jantar Mantar sees large anti-reservation protest despite Delhi Police warning
item.description: A large crowd gathered at Delhi's Jantar Mantar for a protest. These protesters demanded changes to the existing caste-based reservation system. Delhi Police had clearly stated that no permission was granted for this demonstration. Security forces were deployed and barricades were installed as a precautionary measure. Legal action was warned against those spreading false information about the protest.

item.title: Zuckerberg buys Gothic castle in Ireland, Meta's international HQ, for $35 mn
item.description: Meta CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, and his wife, Priscilla Chan, have acquired the historic Strancally Castle, a stunning Gothic mansion set on an expansive estate in Ireland. This remarkable property will serve as their home base during visits to the nation, which is significant due to Meta's international headquarters being located there. The couple is excited about the opportunity to preserve and nurture this piece of history.

item.title: Five pet swans escaped in Maryland; descendants later neared 4,000
item.description: Five mute swans escaped from an estate in Maryland in 1962 and their descendants multiplied to nearly 4,000 in the Chesapeake Bay region within four decades. The invasive birds eat large amounts of underwater grasses and have also been linked to the displacement of native birds, raising concerns among wildlife managers about their growing impact on the Bay's ecosystem.

item.title: Meet Lianna Genovese, 19, whose simple gadget helps people paint again
item.description: Lianna Genovese, a Canadian student, has created an inspiring device called Guided Hands to assist children with cerebral palsy in expressing their creativity through painting. This innovative tool harnesses arm and shoulder movements, enabling young artists to engage with touch screens effectively. Originally composed of basic materials, Guided Hands has transformed into a recognized commercial assistive technology, earning accolades worldwide for its significant impact.

item.title: How Chile telescope accidentally captured a missing link in astronomy
item.description: An unfinished observatory in Chile has captured dense gas clouds from a dying star. These expelled clouds are now blending back into the Milky Way galaxy. This breakthrough demonstrates how stellar elements are recycled for future celestial bodies. The observatory, MOTHRA, achieved this during calibration tests in November 2025. The findings offer critical new insights into stellar mass loss interactions.

item.title: Congress’s renewed youth outreach: How CJP has forced parties to course correct
item.description: Student protests at Jantar Mantar have prompted political parties to rethink their youth engagement strategies. The Congress party is now focusing on youth issues and expanding its outreach programs nationwide. Rahul Gandhi's recent actions highlight the party's renewed commitment to addressing student concerns. The Congress Working Committee has proposed an education-to-employment roadmap for young people. This shift reflects a broader effort to regain support among the nation's youth.

item.title: Who pays what in a rental home? Property tax, maintenance and utility bills explained
item.description: In India, property taxes are fundamentally the responsibility of the property owner as per municipal regulations. Meanwhile, utility expenses for water and electricity are usually settled by the tenant who consumes these services. Maintenance fees of housing societies are generally charged to owners, but tenancy agreements can sometimes allocate part of these costs to renters. Clarifying these responsibilities helps avoid conflicts between landlords and tenants.

item.description: The Supreme Court disposed of petitions challenging CBFC's certification of "The Kerala Story," ruling them infructuous since the film had already released, while leaving the broader legal question on certification challenges open. Justice Bagchi said this would "await another movie." The court also declined immediate hate speech guidelines, suggesting a separate comprehensive petition instead.

item.description: Weight-loss drugs are creating new demands in beauty and nutrition sectors. Companies are developing products to address nutritional gaps and emerging beauty concerns. Nestle and Tata Consumer are preparing protein and fiber-rich offerings for these consumers. Beauty brands are promoting makeup alternatives to cosmetic procedures for users. This trend is driven by pharmaceutical advancements and growing patient bases.

item.title: 'Being Pullela Gopichand's daughter is a big baggage': Coach B Sumeeth Reddy
item.description: Player-turned-coach Sumeeth Reddy says Gayatri Gopichand's maiden World Championships medal is more than a podium finish. It's the release of years of expectation carried as the daughter of Indian badminton legend and national coach Pullela Gopichand. The team of Gayatri Gopichand and Treesa Jolly defeated China's Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 to secure at least a bronze.

Featuring the legendary Rajinikanth alongside actress Shamna Kasim, the catchy tune boasts an energetic lyrical video. The track is composed and sung by the talented Anirudh Ravichander, with creative lyrics penned by Arunraja Kamaraj. item.title: FDA shuts Radio Club, Khar Gymkhana, McDonald's Colaba kitchens over hygiene violations
item.description: The FDA has temporarily revoked licenses for The Bombay Presidency Radio Club and Khar Gymkhana, citing poor waste management and pest control. The kitchen at The Bombay Presidency Radio Club was notably infested with flies and included dead cockroaches, while a live cockroach issue led to a similar suspension for McDonald's Colaba. These measures highlight serious breaches of hygiene and food safety regulations.
